title: An offer and a fallback
hook: A toy agreement has two possible outcomes. Compare it with a certain outside option.

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Compare the entire proposed agreement with a specified outside option.

misconception: A deal with an attractive best outcome must beat walking away.
objective: Compare the entire proposed agreement with a specified outside option.

claims.text: The named work is Getting to Yes, by Roger Fisher and William Ury, candidate publication year 1981.
claims.source: Roger Fisher and William Ury, Getting to Yes (1981); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Getting to Yes uses the best alternative to an agreement as a benchmark for evaluating a proposed deal.
claims.source: Roger Fisher and William Ury, Getting to Yes (1981); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated payoff model: A inputs [100, 12, 12] yield 12; B inputs [70, 20, -10] yield 11. Prediction correct option 11.00. A gives {A}; B averages {B}. An attractive 20-credit agreement outcome does not by itself beat the certain 12-credit fallback. Probabilities and net values are stipulated; expected value is not a complete negotiation criterion.

claims.text: A toy offer pays 18 with 50% probability and 0 otherwise. What is its expected payoff before comparison with a sure fallback? 0.5 × 18 + 0.5 × 0 = 9; a sure fallback above 9 has the larger monetary expectation.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, payoff, inputs [50, 18, 0], output 9; independent Python recomputation.
